data.name: The Way Of Love: Sub Zero
data.detailed_description:
An operation is being undertaken in the eastern region of the Hawizeh Marshes at night (a relatively remote place from the marshes so that the unique vegetation of this region is visible). The heavy enemy fire, successive explosions, enemy and friendly gunshots from heavy and light machine guns, shrapnel shells and mortar bombs dismember and butcher the soldiers. The sound of cries and groans can be heard from the wounded and the medics throughout the battlefield. The stench of treason hurts one’s nose. Who, and for what purpose, would one betray his own country? One of the most prominent pilots of the Air Force, Asef Mahmoudi, has been taken captive by the Iraqis with a series of critical documents. Any diplomatic move would raise suspicions and is utterly dangerous. The only way is to dispatch one of the most elite members of the commando unit. Rasoul is both passionate and intelligent. Without a doubt, he is the best option. Will he succeed in saving Asef? Will everything go according to plan? I don’t know why the stench of treason still hurts my nose….

Game features:

1. A spy story of a special force agent going into the enemy land until he discovers the truth in fatherland
2. Loyalty to the Adventure genre, more than 10 mini games and tens of environmental puzzles
3. Two main characters
4. Narrating the story in 25 locations and 85 backgrounds with utmost detail
5. 15 characters with more than 80 pages of captivating dialogue
6. More than 20 minutes of motion comic for a more precise narration of the story
7. 60 minutes of engaging goal-oriented music
8. Various stealth gameplays and clothe changings in the form of a classic adventure

data.short_description: In the midst of war, when your most dearest friend is held captive, when sheer silence is your only weapon, and when the fate of war is decided by a number of top secret documents, you have to go on a risky mission - silently and calmly – just like a ghost…

reviews.review:
The Way Of Love: Sub Zero is a narrative-focused point-and-click adventure that places espionage, investigation, and puzzle solving within a wartime setting. Developed by RSK Entertainment and published by Strategy First, it avoids the large-scale combat normally associated with military games and instead builds its experience around infiltration and careful exploration. The result is a fairly traditional adventure game wrapped in a story involving captured personnel, confidential information, betrayal, and a dangerous rescue operation.

The story revolves around Asef Mahmoudi, an Air Force pilot who has fallen into Iraqi hands while carrying highly sensitive documents. Recovering both the prisoner and the information becomes an urgent objective, but handling the situation through conventional channels could create additional complications. An elite commando named Rasoul is therefore assigned to infiltrate hostile territory and conduct the rescue. What initially seems like a relatively direct mission becomes more complicated as questions emerge about how the situation happened and whether someone deliberately betrayed the operation. This mystery gives the narrative a stronger investigative element and provides motivation beyond simply reaching the captive.

Gameplay follows the structure of a classic point-and-click adventure. Much of the player's time is spent moving through illustrated locations, inspecting objects, interacting with characters, gathering information, and figuring out how different environmental elements relate to one another. The game features dozens of puzzles alongside more than ten mini-games, helping break up the regular exploration. Progress often depends on noticing details and understanding what the game expects rather than demonstrating quick reactions, making patience and observation more valuable than mechanical skill.

Stealth is another component of the experience, although it remains relatively straightforward compared with dedicated stealth games. Rasoul must occasionally avoid detection while moving through dangerous areas, and disguises can become part of successfully navigating restricted locations. These mechanics fit naturally with the undercover premise and help prevent the adventure from feeling like nothing more than a sequence of conversations and inventory puzzles. Players expecting elaborate enemy AI or highly flexible stealth systems, however, should keep expectations modest because these features primarily support the adventure-game framework.

The scale of the presentation is respectable for a smaller production. The journey includes around 25 locations represented through approximately 85 backgrounds, giving the campaign a reasonable amount of environmental variety. Fifteen characters appear throughout the story, while more than 80 pages of dialogue demonstrate how heavily the experience relies on narrative development and conversation. Two principal characters contribute to the overall storyline, providing another layer to the way events are presented.

Story sequences receive additional attention through more than 20 minutes of motion-comic material. These sequences give important scenes greater visual presence and help connect different parts of the plot without requiring fully animated cinematics. The soundtrack also contributes to the atmosphere, with roughly an hour of original music supporting exploration, suspense, and dramatic moments. Neither the audiovisual design nor animation reaches the sophistication of a major-budget adventure, but the game makes reasonable use of its resources and maintains a consistent identity.

Its biggest weakness is that the old-fashioned design can occasionally feel rigid. Puzzle solutions may require following a specific sequence of actions, and the deliberate pace can become frustrating when the next objective is unclear. Players accustomed to modern adventures with extensive guidance and streamlined interaction may find themselves spending considerable time searching backgrounds for the required clue. The stealth sequences similarly provide variety without becoming deep enough to stand as a major attraction on their own.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently not officially rated by Valve, so the game should be considered Steam Deck Unknown or Unverified rather than confirmed Playable or Verified. Its modest system requirements suggest that raw performance is unlikely to be the primary obstacle, but the game was designed around traditional PC controls. Since point-and-click interaction is central to the experience, Steam Deck users may need to configure the trackpads, touchscreen, or custom controller mappings for comfortable play. The absence of an official compatibility rating means a completely trouble-free handheld experience should not be assumed.

Overall, The Way Of Love: Sub Zero is a niche adventure whose strongest qualities come from its unusual wartime espionage setting and commitment to traditional point-and-click mechanics. The combination of environmental puzzles, mini-games, conversations, disguises, stealth sequences, numerous locations, motion-comic storytelling, and an underlying mystery gives it more substance than its modest production values initially suggest. It is best suited to players who enjoy slower adventures where observation and narrative progression matter more than combat. Its dated structure and limited mechanical sophistication prevent it from becoming exceptional, but the focused premise and variety of adventure elements make it an interesting curiosity for genre enthusiasts.

Rating: 6/10
